Start working on Linear ticket eng-1356 by fetching its details and creating a dedicated git worktree.

## Steps

### 1. Validate input
- `eng-1356` should be a Linear ticket ID like `ENG-1271`. If missing or malformed, ask the user.

### 2. Fetch ticket details from Linear
- Use `mcp__linear-server__get_issue` with the issue ID `eng-1356`
- Extract: title, description, and `branchName` (Linear provides this)
- If the Linear tool is unavailable, ask the user for a branch name manually

### 3. Determine branch name
- Use the `branchName` field from Linear if available (it's already formatted correctly)
- Otherwise derive it: lowercase the ticket ID + hyphenated slug of the title
  - Example: `ENG-1271 Implement filter search` → `eng-1271-implement-filter-search`
  - Strip special characters, replace spaces with hyphens, truncate to ~60 chars

### 4. Create git worktree
Run these from the repo root (the main working directory, not an existing worktree):

```bash
# Fetch latest main so the worktree starts from up-to-date origin/main
git fetch origin main

# Check if branch already exists
git branch --list <branch-name>

# Check if worktree already exists
git worktree list | grep <branch-name>
```

- **If worktree already exists**: skip to step 5, just `cd` into `.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`
- **If branch does NOT exist**: `git worktree add -b <branch-name> .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> origin/main`
- **If branch already exists but no worktree**: reset the branch to `origin/main` first, then add the worktree:
  ```bash
  git branch -f <branch-name> origin/main
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> <branch-name>
  ```

### 5. Enter the worktree
**Do NOT use the `EnterWorktree` tool** — it always creates a brand-new worktree and will duplicate the one you just created.

Instead, use `cd` to switch into the worktree directory:
```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<branch-name>
```

All subsequent commands should run from this path.

### 6. Install dependencies and set up the worktree
After entering the worktree, run the following to bootstrap the environment:

```bash
pnpm install
```

This is required because worktrees share git objects but each needs its own `node_modules`.

### 6b. Copy .env files from the main repo into the worktree
`.env` files are gitignored, so each worktree needs its own copies. After `pnpm install`, copy all `.env` files (excluding `.env.example` files) from the main repo root into the matching relative paths in the worktree.

The main repo root is the working directory you were in before entering the worktree (e.g. `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph`).

Run:
```bash
# From the main repo root, find all .env files (not .env.example) and copy them into the worktree
find . -name ".env*" \
  -not -name ".env.example" \
  -not -path "./.git/*" \
  -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
  -not -path "./.claude/worktrees/*" \
  | while read f; do
      dest=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>/$f"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
      cp "$f" "$dest"
    done
```

Report which files were copied so the user can confirm.

### 7. Ask the user which app to start
Ask the user which app they want to run in dev mode. Common options:
- **Roam**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=none pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/roam dev`
- **Obsidian**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=local pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/obsidian dev`
- **None**: just set up the environment without starting a dev server

If the user says Roam, also switch the Roam dev symlink:
```bash
ln -sfn <worktree>/apps/roam/dist ~/roam-ext-dev
```
and remind them to reload the developer extension in Roam.

Run the chosen dev command in the background so the user can continue working.

**Dev server gotchas** (learned the hard way — don't rediscover these):

- The filter flag is `--filter`, not `--F`. Turbo 2.5.6 rejects `--F=roam` outright.
- Prefer `pnpm -C <abs-path> <app> dev` over `turbo dev --filter=<app>`. `turbo dev --filter=roam`
  also runs the `@repo/database#dev` dependency, which requires Docker Desktop plus an explicit
  `SUPABASE_USE_DB`; if Docker isn't running turbo fails the *entire* run even though the app
  itself built fine. Going through `pnpm -C` skips the dependency graph.
- `SUPABASE_USE_DB` must be one of `local | branch | production | none | implicit`
  (see `packages/database/src/dbDotEnv.mjs`). Use `none` for work that doesn't touch the database.
- **Always bake the absolute worktree path into the command.** The Bash tool's cwd resets to the
  main repo between calls, so a backgrounded `pnpm --filter roam dev` with no path silently builds
  the *main repo's* `dist` — not the worktree the symlink points at. `pnpm -C <abs-path>` makes the
  path intrinsic to the command so it can't be dropped.
- After starting, verify before reporting success: confirm the log says `built with 0 errors` **and**
  that `<worktree>/apps/roam/dist` has a fresh mtime. A background task that failed still returns a
  task ID.

### 8. Ingest any saved session context
The branch may have been worked on before (e.g. reset from an existing branch).
Check for recorded session context:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, **read the `CONTEXT_FILE`** and load it as working context
  (`Next step`, `Open questions`, `Key decisions`, `Dead ends`).
- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=no` or the command errors, continue — this is a fresh start.

### 9. Show context
After setup, display:
- Ticket ID and title
- Branch name you're on
- Brief description from the ticket (if available)
- Which app dev server is running (if any)
- If prior session context was found: its `TL;DR` and `Next step`
- A short "ready to work" confirmation
- Remind the user they can run `/checkpoint` to save session context before wrapping up

Clicking it uploads the image and opens the create-node dialog with the type picker enabled and Page and Block hidden.

- [ModifyNodeDialog.tsx](apps/roam/src/components/ModifyNodeDialog.tsx) now renders an image preview when an image URL is passed and returns the chosen node type in its success callback.

Worktree: `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph/.claude/worktrees/eng-1356-implement-image-to-node-conversion-flow-via-icon-button-in` (paths below relative to `apps/roam/`). PR #1427 is open on this branch.

## Context

Trang tested the new hover-button flow and the converted node's page did not contain the image. Requirement: the hover button and right-click **Convert To** must do exactly the same three things: create the node, replace the canvas shape, and put the image into the node page.

What the code does today (shared by both flows, unchanged by the PR):
- Both flows call `renderModifyNodeDialog({ imageUrl, ... })` → `createDiscourseNode({ imageUrl, ... })` (`src/components/ModifyNodeDialog.tsx:419-427`) → `createBlocksFromTemplate` → `handleImageCreation` (`src/utils/createDiscourseNode.ts:43-99`).
- `handleImageCreation` only writes the `![](url)` block when the node type's canvas setting **Key Image** is on (`if (isKeyImage && imageUrl)`, line 67). With Key Image off the image is silently dropped. This gate predates the PR (commit f575944a5) and applies equally to right-click, so the two flows already share one code path; the image is lost whenever the chosen type has Key Image off.
- The "existing node" branch of the dialog (`addImageToPage`, `ModifyNodeDialog.tsx:276-332`) is the inconsistent one: it writes the image block **unconditionally** and only uses Key Image to decide query-builder placement.

So the fix is in the shared code, not in the overlay: make new-page creation behave like `addImageToPage`, so the image always lands on the page for any canvas image conversion, in both flows.

## Implementation

### 1. `src/utils/createDiscourseNode.ts` — always write the image block when `imageUrl` is given
Rework `handleImageCreation`:
- Return early only when `!imageUrl`.
- If Key Image is on **and** `key-image-option === "query-builder"` and `extensionAPI` exists: run the query as today and update the placeholder block; fall back to creating a new block at order 0 when no placeholder is returned.
- Otherwise: create the `![](url)` block at order 0 on the page.
Export `handleImageCreation` so the dialog can reuse it. Keep the function small; no new comments beyond one line noting that Key Image only affects placement, not whether the image is added.

### 2. `src/components/ModifyNodeDialog.tsx` — reuse instead of duplicating
Replace the local `addImageToPage` (`:276-332`) with a call to the exported `handleImageCreation({ pageUid, discourseNodes: getDiscourseNodes(), configPageUid, imageUrl, extensionAPI, text: content.text })`. Behaviour of the existing-node path is unchanged (it already added the image unconditionally). Remove now-unused imports (`resolveQueryBuilderRef`, `runQuery`, `createBlock`, `updateBlock` if no longer referenced).

### 3. No change to the overlay or `uiOverrides.tsx`
Both flows already share `renderModifyNodeDialog` → `createDiscourseNode` and `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode`. After step 1 they produce identical results.

Canvas display stays governed by Key Image: `calcCanvasNodeSizeAndImg` (`src/utils/calcCanvasNodeSizeAndImg.ts`) still returns no `imageUrl` for the shape when Key Image is off, so the node shape shows the image only for types configured to show it. Flag this to Trang in the recap; if she wants the shape to always show the image on conversion, that is a separate, one-line change in `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode`.

### 4. Docs — `apps/website/content/roam/guides/using-the-canvas.mdx:218-230`
- Sentence I added: "…added to the node's page" without the Key Image qualifier (it is now always true).
- Callout: reword to say Key Image controls whether the image is shown on the canvas node, not whether the conversion works.

## Verification
1. `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck`, `pnpm exec eslint` on changed files, `pnpm exec prettier --check`.
2. Dev build (`SUPABASE_USE_DB=none pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/roam dev`) → `built with 0 errors`; confirm `~/roam-ext-dev` still points at this worktree; grep dist for a changed symbol.
3. In Roam (Trang, or me if Chrome automation responds): pick a node type with Key Image **off** and one with it **on**. For each, convert one image via hover button and one via right-click Convert To. Expect: node page contains the `![](url)` block in all four cases; canvas node shows the image only for the Key Image type; Convert To → Block still yields an image block on today's daily page.
4. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm ci:validate` from the worktree root, then push to the PR branch and wait for checks.

Yes. The query-builder placement can only put the image under an H1 block that already exists on the new page, and on a brand-new node the only thing that creates blocks is the node type's template. If the Issue template does not produce the H1 block, the query finds nothing.

Here is the order of operations in the shared code, unchanged from before the PR apart from the fallback:

1. The page is created, then the template blocks are created from the node type's template.
2. The Key Image query is run with the new node's text and uid. It is expected to return the block the image should live under, in your case the H1.
3. If it returns a block, the image markdown replaces or fills that block. If it returns nothing, the code now falls back to inserting the image as the first block. Before my change, this no-match case silently added no image at all, which is why nothing pointed at the misconfiguration earlier.

So two conditions must hold for your setup to work: the Issue template must contain the H1 block, and the query must match that block for a freshly created page.

There is also a pre-existing race worth knowing about. If the template uses SmartBlocks syntax, the template is triggered without waiting for it to finish, and the image query runs immediately afterward. The H1 does not exist yet at that moment, so the query misses even when the template is correct. Use this skill for one complete lifecycle: build `apps/roam`, open an authenticated slot, register `apps/roam/dist`, activate it, verify DG runtime readiness, run an optional caller test, capture proof, and close.

It composes with `dg-roam-playwright-session` for account/profile selection.

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1
```

Use another slot for isolated work:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 2
```

The script builds by default, verifies `window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder`, checks the DG settings UI, and writes proof under `local/roam-playwright/artifacts`.

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1 --test-module ./local/roam-playwright/feature-proof.mjs
```

```js
export default {
  readySelector: "[data-testid='feature-ready']",
  async ready({ page }) {
    return page.evaluate(() => Boolean(window.myFeature?.ready));
  },
  async run({ page, outDir }) {
    await page.getByText("Expected output").waitFor();
    return { assertion: "passed" };
  },
  async cleanup({ page, state }) {
    // Remove only fixtures created by run().
  },
};
```

`run()` starts only after the standard DG runtime proof and any caller readiness hook succeeds. `cleanup()` runs when `run()` started, including after a failed assertion. Return JSON-serializable proof values.

## Options

- `--slot 1|2|3`: Select the Roam account/profile.
- `--skip-build`: Load the existing `apps/roam/dist` without rebuilding.
- `--headed`: Run with a visible Chromium window.
- `--keep-open`: Leave the browser open after loading.

content.text:
It is pre-existing. This PR did not change where the image is placed; it only changed what happens when the query finds nothing. Here is what the live graph showed.

**How query-builder placement works, on main and on this branch.** The code runs the configured query and replaces the text of the first block it returns with the image markdown. It never creates a child block. That logic in [createDiscourseNode.ts](.claude/worktrees/eng-1356-implement-image-to-node-conversion-flow-via-icon-button-in/apps/roam/src/utils/createDiscourseNode.ts) is byte-for-byte the same on main, and the query runner files are untouched by the PR.

**Your Issue query needs a placeholder child that the template does not create.** The query on block `nFs49MWEn` returns a block that is in the page titled NODETEXT, has a parent with heading 1. So it looks for a block *inside* the H1, not the H1 itself. The Issue template's "Key Image" H1 has no children, so there is nothing to find. On main this meant the image was silently dropped. On this branch it falls back to the top of the page, which is what you saw on "[[ISS]] - test test test": image at the top, empty H1 below.

**Even with a placeholder, the lookup would usually miss.** The query runner uses Roam's backend index, not the local one. A scratch test created a page with an H1 and an empty child, then queried it:

| Query | Result |
|---|---|
| Local index, immediately | found the child |
| Backend, immediately | empty |
| Backend, after 3 seconds | found the child |

Conversion runs the query right after creating the template blocks, so the backend has not indexed them yet. Also pre-existing.

**A third pre-existing race.** The Issue template contains a SmartBlock. When the legacy SmartBlock path is taken, the template is triggered without being awaited and the image query runs before any blocks exist.

**Fix I recommend**, in the shared helper so both flows benefit:

- Run the Key Image query against the local index. The query runner already supports a local flag; the helper just needs to pass it through.
- Await the SmartBlock trigger before running the image query.
- On your side, add an empty child block under "Key Image" in the Issue template, since the query is written to return that child. Alternatively I can make the code fall back to creating the image as a child of the returned block when the query returns an H1 directly, but that changes the query contract for every graph.

I left the three scratch test modules under the ignored `local/roam-playwright` directory. Tell me which of the fix options you want and I will implement it on the PR branch.

This is a pre-existing bug, not something the PR introduced. On main, right-click Convert To into an Issue node puts the image as the first block on the page, with the "Key Image" H1 left empty. That is exactly what you saw on the PR build.

I need to correct something I told you earlier. I said main silently dropped the image when the query found nothing. That was wrong. When Key Image is on and the query returns nothing, main's code also creates the image as the first block. The only case where main dropped the image was a node type with Key Image off, and that is the one case this PR changed.

**How main handles it.** Canvas Convert To is the only image-to-node flow on main. It goes through the create node dialog into the same placement code this PR uses. For a query-builder key image, that code runs the configured query and overwrites the text of the first block the query returns. If the query returns nothing, it inserts the image at the top of the page. This logic and the backend query runner are both in the repo's first commit, so they have never changed.

**Why your Issue setup never matches.** I recreated the Issue page structure on scratch pages in the dev graph and ran the same lookup your Issue query performs, then deleted the pages.

| Page structure | Backend, immediately | Local, immediately | Backend, after 3 seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Issue template as configured | none | none | none |
| Same, plus an empty child under the H1 | none | found | found |

Two separate causes show up:

1. **The query looks for a child of the H1, not the H1 itself.** The Issue template's "Key Image" heading has no children, so nothing can ever match.
2. **The query reads Roam's backend index, which lags new blocks.** Conversion runs the query immediately after creating the template, so even a correct placeholder is invisible at that moment. The local index sees it right away.

There is also a third risk that this test did not exercise. The Issue template contains a SmartBlock, and on the legacy SmartBlock path the template is triggered without waiting, so the query can run before the H1 exists.

**Suggested fix**, as a follow-up ticket or on this PR, whichever you prefer:
- Run the key image query against the local index, which the query runner already supports.
- Wait for the SmartBlock template to finish before running the query.
- Add an empty child under "Key Image" in the Issue template, since your query is written to fill that child.
